item.title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization — Sat Oct 3, 5:06 AM
item.description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4) Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!
Source: York University

item.title: De las Nubes a Aquí / From the Clouds to Here — Mon Oct 5, 10:00 AM — Gales Gallery
item.description: Sensorium ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/sensorium/ ), AMPD ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/ ) and York International ( https://www.yorku.ca/international/ ) are thrilled to present: De las Nubes a Aquí / From the Clouds to Here. In May 2026, 23 York University students travelled to Costa Rica to take part in the PANF 3030/5030 Global Eco-Arts Residency Course. This 10-day intensive course comprised a series of workshops, gallery tours, creative class-based exercises, community interactions, and participation in a local community festival at York University’s Las Nubes Eco-Campus and surrounding areas. Through these experiences, students were introduced to themes of environmental and community-based art, food sovereignty, site-specific art, and the ethics of community engagement. De la Nubes a Aquí/ From the Clouds to Here highlights some of the student-created art that was inspired by this course and the Las Nubes Eco-Campus in Costa Rica. item.title: Understanding and Preventing Burnout — Tue Oct 6, 11:00 AM
item.description:
Burnout syndrome, more commonly referred to as burnout, can affect anyone regardless of gender, age, and level of professional responsibility. Today, more than ever, we can better understand this insidious phenomenon that causes so much individual and collective imbalance. To promote both employee and company well-being, this workshop highlights the causes and factors of burnout, identifies its physical, psychological, and behavioural symptoms, and develops strategies to address it. Key Learning Outcomes: – Define work-related stress and understand its impact on individuals and workplace dynamics. – Learn what burnout is, including its phases, causes, and symptoms. – Discover strategies to prevent and recover from burnout and promote a healthier work environment. – Explore various stress management techniques, such as time management, relaxation methods, and visualization exercises. Organized by

item.description:

Through a distinctive blend of legal analysis and Native history, Richotte, Jr. explores when and why this transformation occurred, and what it reveals about constitutional interpretation today.
